name: Gavel
description: A single-file H5 auction app whose world model is the rules of bidding. You never name a price, you name a maximum, and the house bids for you in the smallest step the increment ladder allows — a pound under twenty, two under a hundred, five under two hundred and fifty, and so on. Beat the other bidder's hidden maximum and you lead at their figure plus one step, not at yours; fall short and you are outbid before the screen redraws. Over the top of that sits a reserve you are never shown, only told whether it is met — so a lot can be yours on the screen and still not be sold. 6 screens, 8 lots, nothing random.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

observation.text: engine.a11y(state) — the current bid, the minimum next bid, the ladder and whether the reserve is met all serialise; the rival's maximum never does.
observation.pixels: 390x844 screenshot (browser backend); __ENV__.bounds() maps every test-id to a pixel box
observation.state: engine.snapshot(state) — canonical state plus a derived view keyed by lot title. For the verifier only.

world.ladder: £1 under £20, £2 under £100, £5 under £250, £10 under £500, £20 under £1000, £50 above
world.proxy: a bid is a maximum; if it beats the rival's you lead at rival + one step, otherwise you are outbid at your maximum + one step, capped at theirs
world.reserve: hidden; the app says met or not met and nothing else
world.money: integers in pence, so every resulting price is exact
